Takes the host-supplied subject and universe (CompanyMetrics serde documents; Rust rejects a misspelt key) and edits a RelativeValueReportConfig with the schema form over the generated relative_value_report_config contract: the PeerFilter (every field optional; GICS sectors, industries, countries, ratings, tags and selectors are free text, since Rust declares no list of them), the period basis, the scoring dimensions and the multiple columns, whose choices come from the contract. Compare passes the subject, universe and structurally valid config JSON to the caller (usually the useRelativeValueReport request) and Rust validates them. The native statements_analytics.relativeValueReport result is shown as returned, above the form: the subject, period basis, peer and excluded counts and the composite score and confidence, or Rust's reason for no composite; the comps table with the subject first, marked from Rust's is_subject, and one column per multiple; per multiple, the subject value, percentile, z-score and peer statistics, with a bar per multiple drawn at Rust's percentile; per dimension, its weight, direction, subject values, percentile, z-score, signal (positive meaning cheap), regression and peer statistics, Rust's exclusion reason when the composite leaves it out, and a scatter of Rust's points with the subject marked from each point's is_subject and the line drawn through Rust's fitted values. A null or a live NaN shows as Undefined and -0 as 0. Nothing is computed here. Accepts subject, universe, defaultConfig, onSubmit, report, loading, error, formatNumber, formatPercentile and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: statement-export
visual.docs: Answers what the statement numbers are as a file a spreadsheet can open. Presents a native statements.statementResultToTableWide or statementResultToTableLong TableEnvelope (useStatementResultTable) in Rust's order, with a wide or long switch the host follows. Download CSV writes exactly those cells: RFC 4180 quoting, native column names as the header, every number as its plain String form. A cell Rust holds with no value shows as undefined and is an empty field. Nothing is computed. Accepts layout, onLayoutChange, table, loading, error and density props; no worker or query provider required.

visual.name: statements-workbench
visual.docs: Open on complete host-supplied financial statements with report-style inline editing, a table and CSV export of the shown result, selectable periods, configurable native forecast methods, service-supplied roll forward with a native review since the last roll forward (variance, a variance bridge and a forecast backtest over the newly reported periods, offering only nodes present before and after), formula-backed calculated metrics with the active period's native credit assessment and P&L summary and, in a disclosure, a native normalization of the reported result (adjusted EBITDA: a NormalizationConfig editor and statements.normalize's base-to-adjusted bridge) and, in another, the native debt stack (statements_analytics.capitalStructureSummary: leverage and coverage through each payment class and the maturity wall; a model with no capital structure shows Rust's error), a native DCF valuation with its enterprise-value tornado, a native WACC calculator that sets the DCF WACC field on the user's click, and a native LBO in Valuation, a native Monte Carlo of the stochastic forecasts with its percentile fan and breach probability in Monte Carlo, covenant compliance in Covenants (a covenant engine from defaultCovenantEngineJson or a Rust package template, tested by statements_analytics.evaluateCovenants at the end of every result period, with a metric the model lacks returned as Rust's not_found error, and a native breach forecast, statements_analytics.forecastBreaches, under a submitted CovenantForecastConfig), and checks. Scenarios override driver values and whole forecast specs and run natively, with the capital structure priced from the host market when one is supplied; each scenario shows its native lineage, and the active period's deltas against a chosen baseline (its parent by default) come from statements_analytics.scenarioDiff. Below the scenarios, a native sensitivity run ranks driver moves with a tornado, and a native goal seek solves for a driver value on Solve; applying the solved model is a separate, explicit action with no undo. The Annual view rolls results up natively: flows sum, balances take the year end and ratios are recalculated, with per-line methods editable. The schema editor and JSON import are in Advanced. density prop (compact default) sets SurfaceContext and data-density on the root; data-theme is inherited from the host. Host owns data ingestion and persistence. Requires FinstackQueryProvider.
